text: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a severe thunderstorm warning, forecasting heavy rain and strong winds across several states and federal territories until 9 pm today. Issued at 5:50 pm, the alert covers the entire Klang Valley, including Kuala Lumpur, Selangor, and Putrajaya, alongside Penang. Up north, the warning extends to Kedah (Sik, Kuala Muda, Baling, Kulim, and Bandar Baharu). Meanwhile, Perak is set to take a battering, with alerts plastered across Kerian, Selama, Larut Matang, Manjung, Bagan Datuk, Perak Tengah, Hilir Perak, Kampar, Kinta, and Kuala Kangsar. Over in East Malaysia, Sarawak’s Limbang division is on high alert. In Sabah, the stormy weather targets the interior divisions of Sipitang, Tenom, and Pensiangan, sweeping across to the Sandakan division, which includes Tongod, Labuk, Sugut, and Kinabatangan. The national weather bureau triggers these short-term alerts when radar detects imminent thunderstorms with rainfall intensity expected to exceed 20 millimetres per hour. These warnings are highly specific and valid for a maximum of six hours. Residents in the affected zones should stay indoors, avoid parking in low-lying areas prone to flash floods, and steer clear of open spaces. Keep an eye on MetMalaysia’s official channels for real-time updates as the evening progresses.

PUTRAJAYA, Oct 22 — The Supplementary Electoral Roll for September 2026 (DPT BLN9/2026) will be open for review for a period of 30 days, starting today until Nov 20, said Election Commission (EC) secretary Datuk Khairul Shahril Idrus. He said the DPT BLN9/2026, which was gazetted today, includes 44,987 citizens aged 18 and above registered automatically as new voters between Sept 1 and Sept 30, 2026. Additionally, the electoral roll contains 21,720 registered voters who have changed their electoral constituencies, as well as 4,805 voters who have undergone a change in their voter category or status. “The Election Commission (EC) urges citizens aged 18 and above as of the period between September 1 and September 30, 2026 as well as any registered voters who have applied to change their electoral constituency, voter category, or status, to verify their names in the Supplementary Electoral Roll (DPT) for September 2026 (DPT BLN9/2026). “Should they find that their names are not listed in the DPT BLN9/2026, they may file a claim by completing Form C via the online application at https://myspr.spr.gov.my, or by visiting the relevant State Election Office,” the statement said today. He said verification can be conducted through four channels: the EC portal at https://www.spr.gov.my or https://myspr.spr.gov.my; the online application at https://myspr.spr.gov.my; the MySPR Semak mobile application; or by calling the Voter Registration Inquiry line at 03-8892 7218. “Furthermore, any registered voter in a specific electoral constituency who, upon verification, wishes to object to the inclusion of a voter who has transferred into their constituency may do so by completing Form D via the online application at https://myspr.spr.gov.my, or by visiting the relevant State Election Office. “Form C and Form D can also be downloaded from the EC portal at https://www.spr.gov.my. These must be submitted to the respective State Election Director, along with the payment of the required objection fee, during office hours on any working day throughout the verification period for the DPT BLN9/2026,” he said. He said for any inquiries regarding the review of the Electoral Roll (DPT) for September 2026 (BLN9/2026), the public may visit the official Election Commission (EC) portal at https://www.spr.gov.my, contact the EC at 03-8892 7218, or reach out to any state election office. — Bernama

SEREMBAN, Oct 22 — The man suspected of murdering his wife, a Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) officer, at their residential quarters near Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) in Nilai on Oct 15 has had his remand extended for another seven days. Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the suspect would remain in remand until Oct 29, while the case was being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code. “The extended remand period begins today and runs until Oct 29,” he told reporters. A post-mortem found that the woman died from pressure on her neck. The examination also revealed three stab wounds, two to the abdomen and one to the right cheek. The woman, in her 30s, was found dead at the quarters after allegedly being stabbed by her husband, reportedly following a misunderstanding. Police received a report on the incident at 9.30 pm after the husband surrendered at the Bandar Baru Salak Tinggi Police Station in Sepang, Selangor, and reported his wife’s death. — Bernama

KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — Wawasan information chief and Machang MP Wan Ahmad Fayhsal Wan Ahmad Kamal has urged Putrajaya to maintain Digital Nasional Bhd’s (DNB) Western technology stack, saying it is needed to balance the growing role of Chinese technology in Malaysia’s 5G and AI infrastructure. Wan Fayhsal made the call in the Dewan Rakyat while Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who is also the Tambun MP, was present in the chamber. He said DNB’s Ericsson-based network was now Malaysia’s main Western technology counterweight, following U Mobile’s selection of Huawei for the country’s second 5G network. He said the need to retain that balance had become more pressing as the government considers Huawei’s Ascend 910C chips for its proposed sovereign AI cloud, which could eventually handle sensitive government data. “DNB was established by the Perikatan Nasional government in 2021. Now there are two paths, namely DNB with Ericsson and U Mobile with Huawei,” he said during his Budget 2027 debate. “This is a good thing because Malaysia can benefit from Western and Eastern technology, as stressed by Tambun previously.” Wan Fayhsal said Malaysia should not allow one technology ecosystem to become dominant across its critical digital infrastructure. “I hope the government can retain both systems because, in my discussions with ambassadors from Europe and other Western countries, they want Malaysia to provide truly sovereign digital infrastructure so that they can invest in sensitive sectors,” he said. The MP said keeping DNB on Western technology was therefore about more than 5G coverage or speed. It would give Malaysia and foreign investors a credible alternative for operations involving sensitive data. He said the government’s proposed sovereign AI cloud made this consideration more urgent. The government had announced a proposed RM2 billion allocation through the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) to establish the cloud under Budget 2026, with the initiative repeated in Budget 2027. Wan Fayhsal said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil had stated that work was under way to protect government data. “Huawei Ascend 910C chips are being considered, and Telekom Malaysia (TM) has been selected to manage this project,” he said. “The question is whether the government has carried out a risk assessment on the suppliers who will be used to handle national data. “How will the government manage sensitivities related to digital sovereignty?” He said the issue was whether Malaysia was building enough safeguards and alternatives as Chinese technology takes a greater role in the country’s digital ecosystem. “The minister said work is ongoing to protect government data,” he said. “The government must explain whether it has conducted a risk assessment of the suppliers.” Wan Fayhsal did not call for Chinese technology to be excluded. Instead, he said Malaysia should preserve both Western and Chinese technology pathways, so the country is not dependent on any one supplier or geopolitical bloc. “Malaysia can benefit from Western and Eastern technology,” he said. Maintaining DNB’s Ericsson-based stack, he added, would ensure that Malaysia retains a meaningful Western option while U Mobile’s Huawei-backed 5G network and the proposed sovereign AI cloud expand the role of Chinese technology in critical national infrastructure.

PUTRAJAYA, Oct 22 — Malaysia will introduce several transformative measures to strengthen efforts to tackle transboundary haze when it chairs the Sub-Regional Ministerial Steering Committee (MSC) on Transboundary Haze Pollution next year. Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said his ministry was conducting studies and drafting several new initiatives to ensure more effective and concrete action to address the recurring haze problem. “Malaysia will take over the MSC chairmanship next year, and we are studying and planning several new initiatives to strengthen Asean-level efforts to tackle the haze problem. “We hope to take more effective and concrete measures when we chair the MSC,” he told a press conference on the latest haze situation here today. He said Malaysia proposed two key initiatives at the Asean ministerial meeting on July 9: science diplomacy, to ensure planning, action and spending to tackle haze are based on scientific data, enabling more targeted fire prevention and suppression efforts, and the setting up of a sustainable haze fund. “The proposed sustainable haze fund, if approved, would serve as an Asean-level mechanism to help member states strengthen prevention, preparedness and monitoring measures,” he said. He said most fires involved extremely dry peatland, where they could spread underground undetected for weeks or months, highlighting the need to study new technologies, including dry ice-based methods, to improve firefighting efforts. In a related development, Arthur said Malaysia had also introduced the Malaysian Community Multiscale Air Quality Model (CMAQ), which can forecast potential air pollution and haze up to five days in advance. He said the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) had developed the platform to provide detailed air quality forecasts for Malaysia and the wider Southeast Asian region. “We hope other countries will also adopt the system so that the public can plan and prepare up to five days in advance,” he said, adding that the platform began operating this year and is open to the public and Asean member states. On the haze situation, Arthur said the transition to the Northeast Monsoon, expected to begin in late October, could alter the movement of transboundary haze currently affecting several areas in the south of the country, particularly Sarawak and Johor. He said shifts in wind direction during the Northeast Monsoon could carry haze to other areas, easing its impact on areas currently affected, noting that haze drifting northwards from the south had significantly affected southern Sarawak, Johor and Singapore. However, Arthur said Malaysia faced a greater risk of transboundary haze as the Super El Niño phenomenon was forecast to intensify from this month until January 2027, increasing the likelihood of forest and peatland fires in the region. He said the El Niño phenomenon is expected to persist until mid-2027, with the year potentially among the hottest on record, bringing increasingly erratic rainfall, a higher risk of drought and more hotspots and fires that could worsen the haze. “We also forecast that next year could be among the hottest on record, with temperature anomalies exceeding 2°C,” he said, adding that the government had taken into account the experience of the 2015-2016 Super El Niño, when rainfall decreased by up to 30 per cent in peninsular Malaysia and 45 per cent in Sabah. He said prolonged hot and dry conditions would not only increase the risk of forest and peatland fires but could also affect agriculture, food security, water supplies and public health. — Bernama

TEHRAN, Oct 22 — Iran’s Revolutionary Guards on Thursday threatened to strike American bases across the Middle East if the US military continues to escort ships through the Strait of Hormuz. “The US military must know that if this trend continues, the conflict will extend to its bases in the region,” the Guards, the ideological arm of Iran’s military, said in a statement on their Sepah News website. “This is a serious warning,” they added. Iran claims control over Hormuz, a strategic shipping route through which one-fifth of the world’s oil supplies passed before war broke out in February. It regularly attacks ships that attempt to navigate the strait without its authorisation. But the US military has been escorting vessels through the waterway in increasing numbers, with Iran responding by stepping up attacks. Four ships were hit in the area overnight as they attempted to pass through the wider Gulf, Iranian forces said on Thursday. Washington has also been maintaining a naval blockade on Iranian ports in an attempt to squeeze the country’s economy, while negotiations to end the conflict are deadlocked. Hormuz, bordered to the north by Iran and to the south by Oman, is only about 30 kilometres (19 miles) wide at its narrowest point and is a critical route for ships carrying oil and gas from energy-rich Gulf countries. — AFP

PASIR MAS, Oct 22 — Eleven police reports regarding damage to concertina wire fences at 13 illegal crossing points around Rantau Panjang were recorded between March 27 and October 12. Bukit Aman Internal Security and Public Order Department (PGA) Deputy Director Datuk Suzrin Mohamad Rodhi said the damage was believed to have been deliberately done to open up pathways for smuggling activities and cross-border crimes. He added that the records of the PGA Southeast Brigade up to October 22 showed that the damage involved cutting, vandalising, and sabotaging the fences, with the damaged length estimated to be between two and five metres at each location. “Any individuals detected committing the offence will be arrested, and further legal action will be taken,” he told reporters after conducting an inspection at an illegal crossing point near Jeram Perdah, Rantau Panjang, here, today. Suzrin said his team constantly updates field information alongside the National Security Council and the police contingent regarding fence-cutting incidents in the border areas. He added that on-duty personnel also took the initiative to tie back or repair the damaged fences to restore security control at the affected locations, in addition to channelling information to relevant parties for continuous monitoring. “Enforcement actions are also being carried out by the PGA together with the relevant District Police Headquarters to address these incidents and ensure that border security remains preserved,” he said. — Bernama * Editor’s note: PGA stands for Pasukan Gerakan Am, or the General Operations Force.

MELAKA, Oct 22 — Candidates and political parties intending to use drones during the Melaka State Election campaign must first obtain approval from the relevant authorities and cannot deploy the devices indiscriminately. Melaka police chief Datuk Dzulkhairi Mukhtar said drone operations were subject to regulatory controls by the relevant authorities, including the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM). “Political parties cannot simply use equipment such as drones, as approval from the relevant agencies is required. “Even the police must obtain approval before using drones for operational purposes,” he told reporters after attending a briefing on the 16th Melaka State Election for political party representatives at the Melaka Police Contingent Headquarters here today. He said Melaka police would deploy about 3,400 personnel to ensure security and public order throughout the election period, including an additional 1,500 personnel from outside the state to support operations. “The deployment of these reinforcements will be coordinated by Bukit Aman. “The police will also use technology, including closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras and drones operated by a special team, to help ensure the smooth conduct of the election,” he said. Dzulkhairi also reminded all political parties and candidates to avoid raising issues involving race, religion and royalty (3R), spreading defamatory allegations or engaging in actions that could disrupt public order during the campaign period, which begins on Oct 31. “The police will remain vigilant on matters concerning security and public order, while issues involving 3R and social media content will be referred to the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) for investigation,” he said. He said police had so far received two reports involving political parties, lodged on Oct 14, concerning the vehicle-free zone in Banda Hilir and an issue involving a Rohingya ethnic school, even though the nomination process had yet to take place. “Both cases are still under investigation under Section 500 of the Penal Code and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998,” he said. In a related development, Dzulkhairi said a total of 2,764 early voters, including postal voters from the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), had been recorded for the Melaka state election scheduled for Nov 10. Earlier, 140 political party representatives from across Melaka attended the briefing, which also involved representatives from MCMC and the Election Commission (EC). Dzulkhairi said the briefing was aimed at helping political parties understand the procedures and regulations they must comply with throughout the election period, including requirements for campaign permits. “For permit applications, the police will call in candidates’ representatives according to their respective districts to facilitate early applications, making it easier to conduct campaign activities,” he said. — Bernama

JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 22 — A total of 43 individuals, including three Malaysians, were fined between RM1,000 and RM9,000 by three Magistrates’ Courts here today for using forged identity cards or copies of identity cards belonging to other people. Of the total, 35 were charged with using copies of other people’s identity cards, while the remaining eight were charged with using forged identity cards as personal identification documents. The accused, aged between 18 and 49, comprised three Malaysians and foreign nationals from Indonesia and the Philippines. They were sentenced after pleading guilty to the charges, which were read out separately before Magistrates Nurzihan Abdul Rehman, A. Shaarmini and Atifah Hazimah Wahab. The courts also ordered them to serve jail terms ranging from one to six months if they failed to pay their respective fines. The offences were committed at two factories, Gorin Technical Industry (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd and Masimo Medical Technologies (M) Sdn Bhd, located in the MIEL and Pasir Gudang industrial areas, between 10 am and 8 pm on Oct 20. The charges were framed under Regulation 25(1)(e) of the National Registration Regulations 1990 (2007 Amendment), which provides for a maximum jail term of three years, a fine of up to RM20,000, or both upon conviction. The prosecution was conducted by National Registration Department prosecuting officers Mohd Ramzi Adnan, Noorleelawathi Man and Md Shahedan Md Taib. Ten of the accused were represented by lawyers Amir Haikal, Jackson Danial, Heng Wang Qian Wei, Rashidah Baharom and Muhd Akmal Mazlan, while the remaining accused were unrepresented. — Bernama

KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — The Communications Ministry is considering conducting a dedicated study to gauge public understanding of the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) and the history of Malaysia’s formation. Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching said neither the ministry nor its agencies, including the Malaysian Information Department (Japen), had conducted a baseline study for this purpose. She said she was prepared to bring the proposal to the ministry and Japen for further consideration. “At present, neither RTM nor Japen has conducted a survey to measure public understanding of MA63 and the formation of Malaysia. “I will bring the proposal back to the ministry for further discussion with Japen to determine whether the department can conduct the survey,” she said during the question-and-answer session in the Dewan Rakyat today. She was responding to a supplementary question from Isnaraissah Munirah Majilis (Warisan-Kota Belud) on whether the ministry was prepared to conduct a perception study to gauge public understanding, particularly in the Peninsula, of Sabah and Sarawak’s rights under MA63. On existing public information efforts, Teo said Japen had uploaded 115 posts, including 21 creative content pieces, on its official social media channels about the formation of Malaysia and the implementation of MA63. — Bernama * Editor’s note: Japen stands for Jabatan Penerangan Malaysia in Malay, or the Malaysian Information Department in English.

PUTRAJAYA, Oct 22 — Malaysia urges Indonesia to take firm and effective action to tackle fires contributing to transboundary haze pollution, which is affecting air quality and public well-being in Malaysia. Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said Malaysia respected its good diplomatic relations with Indonesia but reserved the right to demand appropriate action to ensure its people could enjoy clean air. “Malaysia’s stance is clear. “We respect our good relations with Indonesia, but we also have the right to demand effective action when cross-border pollution affects our people. “The fires must be controlled, pollution must be reduced and the people must be protected,” he said at a press conference on the latest haze developments here today. Arthur said Malaysia had held several consultations with Indonesia and offered assistance, including assets and personnel, to expedite firefighting efforts in affected areas. He said the offer was also conveyed by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto. Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi also raised the matter during his official visit to Indonesia. Arthur said Indonesia had verbally agreed to accept Malaysia’s assistance, but further coordination was still underway pending authorisation for the deployment of assets and personnel. He said Malaysia would raise the transboundary haze issue at the Asean Foreign Ministers’ Meeting in Manila, the Philippines, early next month to seek a more effective regional solution. The government would study the outcome of the meeting before determining its next steps, he added. Arthur said satellite reports on Oct 14 showed widespread clusters of hotspots in southern Sumatra, as well as West Kalimantan, Central Kalimantan and South Kalimantan. He stressed the importance of regional cooperation to ensure fires were controlled at source and prevent haze pollution from continuing to affect neighbouring countries. — Bernama

KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — The Human Resources Ministry (Kesuma) has lodged several official reports with the authorities over alleged attempts to interfere with an ongoing review and investigation at Talent Corporation Malaysia Berhad (TalentCorp). In a statement today, the ministry said the alleged interference involved spreading misleading information, influencing individuals within the agency, and diverting attention from matters under scrutiny. It said such actions could undermine the integrity and independence of the review and investigation. The reports were lodged following the receipt of information and evidence to allow the authorities to conduct a more appropriate and independent investigation. “Kesuma will leave it entirely to the authorities to examine the evidence, establish the facts and take appropriate legal action if warranted,” the statement said. Kesuma and TalentCorp are undertaking organisational reforms to strengthen the agency’s transparency, integrity and accountability. A joint review by TalentCorp’s management and the ministry identified several areas requiring improvement, including provisions in the company’s constitution, compliance with internal policies, internal controls, and integrity and accountability mechanisms. Kesuma stressed that the review must proceed independently, transparently and without undue interference or influence. It said it would not tolerate attempts to exploit positions, influence or connections to compromise the process. “The review and related investigations also involve TalentCorp employees and management. All parties must cooperate fully to ensure the process is conducted fairly and objectively. “Any further action will be determined by the findings of the review and investigations,” it said. Kesuma said TalentCorp’s operations and strategic programmes would continue as usual throughout the process, with the agency to remain focused on its national talent development mandate, including improving graduate employability, developing future-ready skills and strengthening workforce participation. — Bernama * Editor’s note: Kesuma stands for Kementerian Sumber Manusia, or the Human Resources Ministry.

KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — The High Court here today allowed Perikatan Nasional’s (PN) application to stay the Registrar of Societies’ (RoS) decision to revoke the coalition’s registration pending the outcome of its judicial review. Judge Datuk Azizan Md Arshad also granted PN’s application to stay the enforcement of an RoS notice suspending all activities of the political coalition. The decision allows PN to continue its political activities, including contesting the Melaka state election scheduled for November 14. In his judgment, Azizan said there were exceptional circumstances warranting the stay, taking into account the applicants’ involvement in political activities and their rights as party members, elected representatives and Members of Parliament, as submitted by their counsel. “The court finds that no prejudice will arise if this stay is granted, as the political activities of the applicants or Perikatan Nasional can continue to be monitored, and enforcement action can be taken if any activities are found to contravene the laws of the country. “Therefore, the application for a stay of execution is granted until the full disposal of the substantive hearing of this judicial review,” he said. — Bernama

KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook today said the outstanding payment MyEG Services Bhd (MyEG) owes the government has yet to be settled, following the suspension of the company’s services as a Road Transport Department (JPJ) collection agent earlier this month. MyEG is a digital and e-government services provider that was previously tasked with collecting JPJ-related payments. He said the suspension had not disrupted public access to JPJ services, as motorists could continue using alternative channels, including the MyJPJ application, to access their information and carry out transactions. “There has been no disruption to services because JPJ is handling the matter. The public can use MyJPJ and easily access their information. “As for the payment, it has not been made yet,” he told reporters after launching the Masjid Jamek LRT station beautification project here today. JPJ suspended the services of MyEG Sdn Bhd and Zetrix AI Bhd, both under the MyEG Group, effective October 5 after the companies failed to remit RM314 million in government revenue collected between May 19 and September 30. The outstanding amount comprises revenue collected on behalf of the government that had not been transferred to the Transport Ministry’s main collection account. Loke had previously said the ministry would only consider an application to resume operations after the full outstanding amount had been paid. The government took action after the companies failed to settle the arrears despite receiving 35 reminder notices and participating in engagement sessions with the authorities since May. Despite the suspension, JPJ has assured the public that its services remain available through alternative channels, including the MyJPJ application, JPJ Public Portal, counters and kiosks. The suspension covers JPJ services previously offered through the MyEG Group, including transactions involving road tax, driving licences and traffic summonses. The ministry and JPJ have also said they would take appropriate legal action to recover the outstanding government revenue. Note: The Road Transport Department (RTD) is known as Jabatan Pengangkutan Jalan (JPJ) in Malay.

KUCHING, Oct 22 — Police are gathering and verifying information as investigations into the alleged attack on a female teacher at an international school here yesterday morning continue. According to the Sarawak Police Contingent Headquarters, the investigation team is carrying out various investigative measures to ensure the accuracy of the information obtained. In a statement, the contingent said the investigation is ongoing and a press conference is scheduled for October 27, with the time to be announced later. Media representatives with questions were advised to channel them to the contingent beforehand to allow the relevant parties to prepare accurate and comprehensive answers. Police are investigating a case involving a 16-year-old male student who allegedly attacked a teacher with an axe at an international school here. Yesterday, acting Sarawak Police Commissioner DCP Saifullizan Ishak said police received a report of the incident at 8.03am via the MERS 999 emergency line. The teacher reportedly suffered injuries to her hand during the incident. Saifullizan said the case is being investigated under Section 324 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing hurt by dangerous weapons or means, as well as Section 6(1) of the Explosives Act 1957. — The Borneo Post

KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook today welcomed a RM5 million beautification project at the Masjid Jamek LRT station, saying the busy interchange should be more than a transit point and help drive economic activity and tourism in the capital. Loke said the station, which serves thousands of commuters and sits close to historic attractions in the city, was an important gateway for both locals and tourists. “Every ringgit spent must bring tangible benefits to the people. We want to ensure that the improvements go beyond making the station look beautiful, and genuinely improve comfort, safety and convenience for users. “Public transport stations should not merely be places where passengers board and alight from trains, but should also become centres for community activities, commerce and tourism,” he said at the launch of the project today. The project, launched by Prasarana Malaysia Berhad in collaboration with Think City, is the third phase of efforts to rejuvenate the station and its surrounding area, with works expected to be completed by the end of 2027. The RM5 million investment covers four main components: upgrading the area around Jalan Benteng with public and commercial spaces, improving lighting along Jalan Tun Perak, adding greenery to the station platforms and improving wayfinding around the station. Loke said the improvements were timely, given that Masjid Jamek was a major interchange connecting the Kelana Jaya Line with the Ampang/Sri Petaling Line, serving an average of 1.39 million passengers a month. He also joked that its proximity to Dataran Merdeka made it particularly busy during demonstrations, but stressed that its importance extended beyond its role in the city’s transport network. The area holds historical significance as the meeting point of the Klang and Gombak rivers, which marked the beginning of Kuala Lumpur’s development. Loke said the station was also an important gateway to nearby heritage attractions, including Dataran Merdeka, the Sultan Abdul Samad Building and Sultan Abdul Samad Jamek Mosque. He said the beautification project supported the government’s Warisan Kuala Lumpur (Warisan KL) initiative to strengthen the capital’s heritage appeal while connecting public transport users to cultural attractions and commercial activities. Loke also expressed support for plans to introduce more commercial spaces at stations, saying these could create business opportunities, generate income and encourage more people to use public transport. He said such spaces could also provide opportunities for local businesses and brands to showcase Malaysian products and flavours, rather than being dominated by international brands. “We want to see how public transport stations can be transformed from transit points into catalysts for the economy,” he said. Loke added that improving connectivity beyond stations was equally important in encouraging public transport use, particularly through more covered walkways linking stations to surrounding areas. He welcomed efforts under Budget 2027 to increase covered walkways in Kuala Lumpur, saying Prasarana and Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) should work together to identify gaps and ensure pedestrians could move between transport hubs and nearby destinations more seamlessly. He said he had also instructed Prasarana to provide the Transport Ministry with weekly reports on station facilities, including the number of faulty escalators and lifts that were out of service. Loke said station facilities must remain in good condition to ensure a comfortable and reliable journey, adding that the passenger experience should cover the entire trip, from the station entrance to the final destination. Prasarana said the beautification project had been implemented in phases since 2025 and was expected to turn Masjid Jamek into a greener, more user-friendly space with improved commercial facilities, strengthening its role as a community, tourism and commercial hub in central Kuala Lumpur.

KUCHING, Oct 22 — Bandar Kuching MP Dr Kelvin Yii Lee Wuen has urged the public and the media to stop sharing videos of a school violence incident in Kuching, warning that such exposure can lead to a copycat effect. The incident, which occurred yesterday at an international school, involved a 16-year-old student injuring a teacher. “I appeal to everyone, including the media, to stop sharing videos, images, notes or details of this act,” Dr Yii said in a statement. “Research on school violence overseas shows that widely publicised attacks are often followed by similar incidents.” He noted that when an attack is livestreamed and shared thousands of times, the attacker gains the notoriety he may have been seeking. “Every share, however well-meaning, puts more children in danger,” he added. Dr Yii also pointed to a troubling rise in violent incidents involving students since the killing of a student in Bandar Utama in October 2025. He stressed that while guards, fences, and bag checks have their place, they cannot address the negative material children are exposed to online. “If we ignore this factor, we will keep responding to tragedies instead of preventing them,” he said. The MP highlighted that he has consistently pushed for stronger online regulations in Parliament. He noted that just two days before the Kuching incident, he asked the Communications Ministry if the government would extend social media age limits to online gaming platforms. While he welcomed the ministry’s ongoing studies and public consultations on a new Gaming Sub-Code, he stressed that these efforts must be matched with urgency. Citing Australia’s experience, Dr Yii said age limits alone are easily bypassed, pointing out that over eight in ten children under 16 there still use social media despite a ban. “As we roll out our own measures, we must place a firm duty of care on platforms,” he said, urging them to design safer services and stop algorithms from amplifying harmful content. Dr Yii also addressed the cruelty the young suspect faced online prior to the incident, noting that constant mockery from strangers can push youth toward harming themselves or others. He emphasised that the teenager is a minor whose identity must be protected, adding that he should be dealt with through legal and rehabilitative processes rather than an online mob. He called for stronger mental health support and early intervention in schools to recognise warning signs before it is too late. Furthermore, Dr Yii called on the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) to play a more proactive role by working with platforms to detect and block re-uploads of violent footage immediately, rather than waiting for complaints. He suggested establishing a rapid-response protocol for school-related incidents to contain harmful material in the critical first hours. Dr Yii also urged online news portals and social media page owners to prioritise responsibility over viewership. “What is the point of higher viewership and ratings if the price is making our schools less safe?” he questioned. The MP added that he has spoken to Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching and urged the Malaysian Media Council to establish clear guidelines on reporting such incidents. “Protecting our children is a shared duty of government, platforms, schools, parents, the media and every one of us who scrolls, comments and shares,” he said.

SEREMBAN, Oct 22 — The RM1,000 special financial assistance from the Madani Government has brought relief to more than 400 taxi and hire car drivers in Negeri Sembilan, particularly those celebrating Deepavali, by helping them prepare for the festival, Transport Minister Anthony Loke said. He said the aid would help reduce recipients’ financial burden, allowing them to meet the costs of Deepavali preparations and their families’ daily needs. “The RM1,000 may not resolve every problem or fully cover vehicle maintenance costs. “However, I hope the assistance will go some way towards easing their daily expenses, helping them buy groceries, replace tyres or refuel their vehicles so they can continue earning a living. “I promised earlier that the assistance would be delivered before Deepavali. “Today, I am handing it over ahead of the festival so that you can put it towards your Deepavali expenses,” he said at a ceremony for taxi, hire car and school bus drivers at the Seremban City Council Hall today. Loke said the next phase of the assistance would be paid directly into the bank accounts of other eligible recipients nationwide through electronic funds transfer. He said the Ministry of Transport (MOT) would continue supporting taxi drivers through its transformation programme to keep them competitive in the public transport industry, including by working with Proton to lower the cost of new vehicles and providing financing facilities and rebates to ease their financial burden. He said more than 100 vehicles had been booked under the programme, which seeks to boost drivers’ earnings by offering advertising space inside vehicles and using apps to connect them with passengers. In a related development, Loke said the government would continue to issue special vehicle registration number series, typically two to three a year, but had no plans to introduce numbers featuring specific names or words, opting to retain the existing alphanumeric system. Loke said the MOT had decided to retain the country’s long-standing vehicle registration system, despite the potential for personalised number plates to generate additional government revenue. Meanwhile, taxi driver L. Jagathesan, 68, who has worked in the industry for 30 years, said the incentive was the biggest he had received and would go towards his Deepavali expenses. Port Dickson taxi driver M. Selvaraju, 66, who has worked in the industry for 37 years, said he appreciated the government’s gesture towards taxi drivers and hoped similar efforts would continue. Driver Muhammad Auzai Azman, 28, who has been in the profession for two years, said the assistance helped drivers like him meet their daily needs. — Bernama

KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — The Air Pollutant Index (API) readings issued by the Department of Environment (DOE) remain the government’s official reference for determining air quality and managing haze. Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said the official API was calculated based on the concentrations of six major pollutants monitored around the clock through 68 automatic air quality monitoring stations nationwide. He said the stations used measurement equipment and technical methods recognised by the United States Environmental Protection Agency, with procedures in place to ensure the accuracy and reliability of the data. “Station operations include equipment maintenance, calibration, instrument performance checks and quality assurance procedures to ensure that the data used to calculate the official API are accurate and reliable,” he said during the Minister’s Question Time in the Dewan Rakyat today. Arthur was answering a question from Manndzri Nasib (BN-Tenggara), who wanted to know how the government ensured that Malaysia’s official API readings were accurate, transparent and trusted by the public. He said the stations operated under a Quality Assurance Project Plan (QAPP), which included daily automated zero and span checks, periodic calibration using standard gases traceable to international metrology standards under the National Institute of Standards and Technology, and regular performance audits. Data collected were also monitored continuously through the Environmental Data Centre to detect changes in readings, assess equipment performance and enable corrective action in the event of disruptions or irregularities. Arthur said the official API was updated hourly, while the calculations for PM2.5 and PM10 were based on their 24-hour moving average concentrations, in line with World Health Organisation standards and practices adopted by international environmental agencies. On differences between official API readings and those displayed on platforms such as the Air Quality Index (AQI) and other independent applications, he said these did not necessarily mean that the official readings were inaccurate. “Differences may arise because these platforms use different scales, thresholds, categories, averaging periods, update times and data sources,” he said, adding that some also relied on low-cost sensors or estimates derived from models and satellite data. He explained that satellite data measured particle concentrations in the atmosphere rather than actual air quality at ground level, where people breathe. Such readings could also be affected by cloud cover and atmospheric humidity. Meanwhile, Arthur said the ministry was open to improving the National Haze Action Plan to ensure that coordination mechanisms and protective measures remained relevant as haze conditions changed. “This is important to ensure that the actions of the various agencies are better coordinated, particularly when API readings reach unhealthy or very unhealthy levels, to protect public health and well-being,” he said. On measures to address haze and open burning, Arthur said the government maintained a zero-tolerance approach towards open burning. The DOE had taken 3,433 enforcement actions related to open-burning incidents between August and October this year, he added. — Bernama

Wan Fayhsal berkata dasar berkenaan memberi Malaysia akses kepada dua ekosistem teknologi 5G berbeza, dengan Digital Nasional Bhd (DNB) menggunakan peralatan Ericsson bagi rangkaiannya manakala U Mobile menggunakan teknologi Huawei. “DNB ditubuhkan di bawah Kerajaan Perikatan Nasional pada 2021. Sekarang ini kita dua laluan iaitu DNB bersama Ericsson untuk 5G kita dan U Mobile memilih Huawei. “Ini satu perkara yang baik kerana Tambun (Anwar) pernah kata, Malaysia patut dapat manfaat daripada teknologi Barat dan Timur,” katanya ketika membahaskan Belanjawan 2027 di Dewan Rakyat. Anwar yang juga Ahli Parlimen Tambun, berada di Dewan Rakyat ketika Wan Fayhsal membuat kenyataan itu. Ketua penerangan Wawasan itu menggesa kerajaan mengekalkan dasar berkenaan supaya Malaysia tidak terlalu bergantung kepada hanya satu ekosistem teknologi. “Saya harap kerajaan dapat mengekalkan kedua-dua sistem kerana berdasarkan perbincangan saya dengan duta dari Eropah dan negara Barat lain, mereka mahu Malaysia menyediakan infrastruktur digital yang benar-benar berdaulat supaya mereka boleh melabur dalam sektor sensitif,” katanya. Wan Fayhsal berkata kedua-dua sistem perlu dikekalkan bukan sahaja untuk meningkatkan liputan dan kualiti rangkaian 5G, tetapi juga bagi meningkatkan keyakinan pelabur, menjaga kedaulatan digital serta mengukuhkan keupayaan negara menyediakan infrastruktur dipercayai bagi operasi sensitif. Menurutnya, prinsip sama juga perlu digunakan dalam cadangan kerajaan membangunkan awan AI berdaulat yang boleh menempatkan data sensitif kerajaan. Kerajaan sebelum ini mengumumkan cadangan peruntukan RM2 bilion menerusi Suruhanjaya Komunikasi dan Multimedia Malaysia (SKMM) untuk membangunkan awan berkenaan dalam Belanjawan 2026, sebelum inisiatif itu ditegaskan semula dalam Belanjawan 2027. Wan Fayhsal berkata Menteri Komunikasi Fahmi Fadzil sebelum ini memaklumkan usaha sedang dilakukan untuk melindungi data kerajaan. Katanya, cip keluaran Huawei turut dipertimbangkan bagi projek itu manakala Telekom Malaysia dipilih untuk menguruskannya. “Cip Huawei Ascend 910C sedang dipertimbangkan dan Telekom Malaysia dipilih untuk menguruskan projek ini,” katanya. “Persoalannya, adakah kerajaan sudah melakukan penilaian risiko terhadap pembekal yang akan digunakan untuk mengendalikan data negara? “Bagaimana kerajaan akan menguruskan isu sensitif berkaitan kedaulatan digital?” Wan Fayhsal berkata kerajaan tidak perlu menolak teknologi China, tetapi perlu memastikan peranannya yang semakin besar dalam infrastruktur 5G dan AI negara tidak menyebabkan Malaysia kehilangan pilihan teknologi lain yang berdaya maju. “Malaysia boleh mendapat manfaat daripada teknologi Barat dan Timur,” katanya. Menurutnya, mengekalkan rangkaian DNB berasaskan Ericsson bersama rangkaian U Mobile yang menggunakan Huawei memberi Malaysia fleksibiliti untuk memanfaatkan kedua-dua ekosistem, sekali gus mengelakkan kebergantungan kepada satu pembekal atau blok teknologi sahaja.

Wan Fayhsal said the policy gives Malaysia access to two distinct 5G technology ecosystems, with Digital Nasional Bhd (DNB) utilising Ericsson equipment for its network while U Mobile relies on Huawei technology. “DNB was established by the Perikatan Nasional government in 2021. Now there are two paths, namely DNB with Ericsson and U Mobile with Huawei,” he said when debating the 2027 budget in the Dewan Rakyat. “In hindsight, this is a good thing because Malaysia can benefit from Western and Eastern technology, as stressed by Tambun previously.” Anwar, the Tambun MP, was present in the chamber during Wan Fayhsal’s remarks. The Wawasan information chief urged the government to maintain its current policy rather than allow Malaysia to become reliant on only one technology ecosystem. “I hope the government can retain both systems because, in my discussions with ambassadors from Europe and other Western countries, they want Malaysia to provide truly sovereign digital infrastructure so that they can invest in sensitive sectors,” he said. Wan Fayhsal said it was important for Malaysia to retain both systems, not only to enhance 5G coverage and network quality, but also to bolster investor confidence, safeguard digital sovereignty, and strengthen the country’s ability to provide trusted infrastructure for sensitive operations. Wan Fayhsal said the same principle should apply to the government’s proposed sovereign AI cloud, which could host sensitive government data. The government had previously announced a proposed RM2 billion allocation through the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission to establish the cloud under Budget 2026, and reiterated the initiative in Budget 2027. He said communications minister Fahmi Fadzil had stated that work was under way to protect government data, adding that chips produced by Huawei were being considered for the project, with Telekom Malaysia Bhd selected to manage it. “Huawei Ascend 910C chips are being considered, and Telekom Malaysia has been selected to manage this project,” Wan Fayhsal said. “The question is whether the government has carried out a risk assessment on the suppliers who will be used to handle national data. “How will the government manage sensitivities related to digital sovereignty?” Wan Fayhsal said the government need not reject Chinese technology, but must ensure that its growing role in the country’s 5G and AI infrastructure does not come at the expense of meaningful alternatives. “Malaysia can benefit from both Western and Eastern technology,” he said. Maintaining DNB’s Ericsson-based stack alongside U Mobile’s Huawei-backed network would give Malaysia the flexibility to draw from both ecosystems while avoiding dependence on any single supplier or technology bloc, he said.

The mayor of Belen and two young women visited a care home on their trip to Nanmoku, a village of just 1,300 people in Gunma Prefecture, greeting the elderly with broad smiles as some looked on slightly puzzled. “From the moment I arrived, I began to admire everything about this place,” 19-year-old student Wendy Sangama told AFP during a week-long tour of Japan that followed the signing of a sister-city agreement between her hometown and the village last year. “And yes, it’s a town where I could see myself living and settling down,” she said. The village is the oldest municipality in Japan, with 70% of its residents aged 65 or above. A 2014 think tank report described it as “most at risk of disappearing”. The main street along the Nanmoku River is lined with houses and shops, some abandoned, and appeared largely deserted on the rainy weekend AFP visited. Village officials hope the sister-city agreement, which promotes cultural and people-to-people ties, will ultimately attract young people from Belen to live in Nanmoku, although how they might obtain residency remains unclear. While Peru has the world’s third-largest population of Nikkei – Japanese immigrants and their descendants – Nanmoku mayor Saijo Hasegawa told AFP the pact was down less to strategy than to a chance meeting with a Japanese-Peruvian businessman. “The village needed “to broaden its horizons and attract more residents, including foreigners”, no matter where they came from,” he said. “Without them, we could reach a point where even public transportation stops operating,” he added. ‘No work’ Despite its rapidly ageing population and labour shortages, opposition to immigration is growing within Japan, prompting a push by prime minister Sanae Takaichi for tighter regulations on foreign nationals. Nanmoku has tried various initiatives to attract young people from elsewhere in the country, but employment opportunities remain scarce, and farmland is limited in the mountainous area. “Around 60 people die each year here, and just two or three babies are born,” Hasegawa said. Belen, meanwhile, is young. The impoverished district of Iquitos, a remote Amazonian city in northeastern Peru, has a median age of about 27 years old. Home to more than 60,000 residents, the “Venice of Latin America” – accessible only by plane or boat – is filled with wooden houses built on stilts to withstand seasonal flooding. “I think the young people would be more enthusiastic about wanting to settle in other cities because of the economic situation we have,” mayor Lina Arista Lopez told AFP. The district’s residents rely largely on informal trade and agriculture, growing crops such as yuca, rice and corn. “We have a harsh reality in Belen,” Lopez said. “There is no work,” Lopez added. Ketsi Yahuarcani, a 23-year-old student, called the visit to Nanmoku “incredible”, citing the sense of warmth she felt. “If I had the opportunity to settle here, I would,” she said. Sangama, the other student, said moving to the Japanese village could be “a better option” if it allowed them to build a brighter future and support their families back home. Not being able to see her family regularly, however, would “certainly be a challenge”, she conceded. Putting down roots While municipalities near Nanmoku have accepted foreign workers, particularly caregivers, it has typically been via short-term programmes for skilled workers and technical interns. Mayor Hasegawa said his vision was different. Rather than attracting people who stay only a few years for work, he hopes to welcome residents of Belen as fellow villagers ready to build long-term lives in Nanmoku. “The approach of simply bringing in workers from an agency just because we’re short-staffed isn’t right for our village,” he said. Yuki Wanibuchi, 34, who moved to Nanmoku several years ago from the Kyoto area, said potential newcomers would face hurdles, including the language barrier. “You cannot live here without a car, and getting a driver’s licence will require Japanese skills,” Wanibuchi said. “But personally, I think it’s more interesting when people from different backgrounds come here to live.” Hiroshi Ihara, an 87-year-old villager, told AFP he had watched his community grow greyer and greyer, with young people, including his three children, moving to bigger cities to make a living. “I want more younger people to come and live in the village,” he said. “The Japanese population is shrinking. I think it would be best if people from overseas could come here and do what they can to support us,” he added.

Ketika membahas Belanjawan 2027 di Dewan Rakyat, Jalaluddin (BN-Jelebu) dicelah Rosol Wahid (PN-Hulu Terengganu) yang bertanya sama ada ketiadaan barisan exco baharu akan merencatkan pembangunan negeri itu. “Hulu Terengganu, jangan risau…(perkara itu) akan selesai. Biar Negeri Sembilan selesaikan masalah negeri Sembilan. Insya-Allah, (marilah kita) doa sama-sama,” katanya tanpa memberikan sebarang tempoh masa. Negeri Sembilan tiada barisan exco sejak 20 Sept lalu, selepas Yang Dipertuan Besar, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir membatalkan pelantikan 10 exco kerana melanggar sumpah jawatan mereka. Pelantikan itu dibatalkan susulan kenyataan dikeluarkan mereka lima hari sebelumnya yang menyokong satu deklarasi menyingkirkan Tuanku Muhriz sebagai Yang Dipertuan Besar. Bekas menteri besar, Aminuddin Harun, yang kini ketua PKR Negeri Sembilan, berkata ketiadaan barisan exco menjejaskan urusan pelaburan dan perniagaan yang memerlukan kelulusan kerajaan negeri. Beliau berkata, kerajaan negeri tidak dapat berfungsi seperti biasa hampir dua bulan selepas mengambil alih pentadbiran, dengan keputusan penting berkaitan dasar serta kelulusan masih tertangguh. Dari segi ekonomi, Jalaluddin berkata, ekonomi Negeri Sembilan perlu terus dibangunkan dan statistik Jabatan Perangkaan menunjukkan nilai ekonomi negeri itu mencecah RM58 bilion tahun lalu. Beliau mencadangkan Putrajaya menyokong pembangunan koridor ekonomi negeri itu dengan menyediakan rangkaian pengangkutan dan utiliti mencukupi, kemudahan logistik serta tenaga kerja mahir. Perkeso untuk pelatih industri Jalaluddin turut menyarankan pelajar menjalani latihan industri dalam sektor industri berat layak menerima caruman Pertubuhan Keselamatan Sosial (Perkeso). Beliau merujuk satu kes di kawasan Parlimennya, di mana seorang pelajar sedang menjalani latihan industri maut dalam nahas jalan raya ketika dalam perjalanan ke tempat kerja. Keluarga mangsa tidak dapat menuntut pampasan kerana pelajar itu bukan pencarum Perkeso. Kes sedemikian, katanya, boleh membebankan keluarga berpendapatan rendah yang bergantung harapan kepada anak untuk mengubah nasib keluarga.

The “Board of Peace,” of which Indonesia is a key troop-contributing member, was unveiled by Trump in January to address global conflicts typically handled by the UN. The world’s largest Muslim-majority nation has also pledged troops to be deployed to Gaza as part of an international stabilisation force. Francesca Albanese, a prominent human rights lawyer known for her vocal criticism of Israel, said in an interview in Jakarta that Indonesia has historically supported the Palestinian cause, but joining the board was dangerous. Indonesia’s Foreign Ministry said on Thursday that Board of Peace discussions remained on hold, reiterating its earlier position. Albanese has drawn the ire of a number of Western capitals. The US has imposed sanctions on her, and others, including her own native Italy, have called for her resignation. “I understand (Indonesia’s) good intentions. I still think that it’s very dangerous, because it risks to normalise a very abnormal mechanism,” she said. Albanese said that, legally, Israel could not have a role in determining the future of Palestinians. Rights experts have criticised the board for not including a Palestinian representative even though it is meant to supervise the temporary governance of a Palestinian territory. The Board of Peace did not immediately respond to a request for comment outside US business hours. Indonesia, which backs a two-state solution and has repeatedly condemned Israeli violence, has drawn criticism from domestic Muslim groups for agreeing to join the board, which also counts Israel as a member. President Prabowo Subianto has vowed to quit if it does not bring benefits to Palestinians, his office has previously said, adding that joining the board would allow Indonesia to push for cessation of violence. Albanese said Indonesia risked compromising its close ties with Palestinians. “It’s very risky to do so when the rules are set by Israel,” she said. Albanese recommended Jakarta join the Hague Group of countries, which includes South Africa and Indonesia’s neighbour Malaysia and seeks to uphold international law and processes, including in the International Criminal Court over Israel’s actions. Trump’s Gaza plan has stalled. A 2025 ceasefire secured the release of the remaining hostages held by Hamas and hundreds of Palestinian prisoners and detainees, but efforts to disarm Hamas and secure an Israeli withdrawal have faltered, while Israeli forces continue near-daily attacks in Gaza. Israel’s government has denied accusations, including by a UN commission and international and Israeli rights groups, that it is committing genocide against Palestinians in Gaza.

The EU unveiled on Tuesday a push to boost Arctic surveillance and expand icebreaker fleets, alluding to China’s growing “strategic ambitions… as it deepens its partnership with Russia”. Europe, China, Russia and the United States are jostling for influence in the polar region that is seen as an important trade route. This summer, a Chinese shipowner began a weekly container service through the Arctic on an express route to Europe, prompting concerns over vessels warming polar ice. Beijing and Moscow agreed this week to “expand cooperation” in Arctic shipping, including increasing the number of routes between Russian and Chinese ports, according to a joint communique released after a meeting between their prime ministers. Asked about the new EU strategy and calls from foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas to bolster the bloc’s defences in the Arctic, China denounced what it called a “Cold War mentality”. “China’s activities in the Arctic are aimed at promoting the Arctic’s peaceful, stable and sustainable development and are in accordance with international law,” foreign ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning said during a regular news conference. “Using Cold War mentality to create factions and incite geopolitical confrontation is not conducive to the peaceful and stable development of the Arctic region,” she said, without naming the EU specifically.

Mengulas saranan Menteri Besar Selangor Amirudin Shari supaya kerajaan memperluas asas hasil negara dan mengenal pasti industri strategik baharu, pemain industri R Jeyenderan berkata Malaysia mempunyai beberapa kelebihan untuk membangunkan sektor terbabit. Katanya, ia termasuk sumber petroleum, kemudahan penyimpanan, rangkaian pelabuhan dan kedudukan strategik di laluan perdagangan utama yang boleh dimanfaatkan untuk membolehkan syarikat tempatan terlibat dalam aktiviti bernilai tambah, bukan sekadar penyedia logistik. Menurutnya, antara bidang boleh diteroka ialah penghasilan minyak bahan api sulfur sangat rendah (VLSFO), yang digunakan kapal bagi mematuhi had kandungan sulfur global 0.50% ditetapkan Pertubuhan Maritim Antarabangsa (IMO) sejak Januari 2020. “VLSFO boleh dihasilkan dengan mencampurkan komponen petroleum yang sesuai sebelum produk itu diuji bagi memastikan ia memenuhi spesifikasi ditetapkan. “Sebagai contoh, syarikat boleh mendapatkan komponen bahan api yang sesuai daripada kilang penapisan atau pembekal petroleum, mencampurkannya mengikut nisbah terkawal dan menguji produk yang dihasilkan bagi memastikan kandungan sulfur serta spesifikasi bahan api lain memenuhi syarat ditetapkan,” katanya dalam kenyataan. Jeyenderan berkata, model itu juga membolehkan Malaysia menerima pelbagai produk petroleum, mencampurkannya mengikut spesifikasi pembeli dan kemudian menjual produk siap kepada pengendali perkapalan. “Pendekatan itu boleh memperluas rantaian nilai industri tempatan, sekali gus menjana pendapatan daripada aktiviti perdagangan, penyimpanan, logistik dan pembekalan bahan api kapal,” katanya. Semalam, Amirudin menggesa kerajaan memperluas asas hasil negara dan mengenal pasti industri strategik baharu yang mampu memberikan pulangan berterusan. Jeyenderan berkata, pembangunan hab bahan api marin juga berpotensi meningkatkan permintaan terhadap perkhidmatan pelabuhan, logistik dan perdagangan petroleum, sekali gus memberi manfaat kepada lebih banyak perniagaan tempatan. Bagaimanapun, katanya industri itu memerlukan garis panduan kawal selia dan operasi yang jelas bagi memastikan proses pengendalian, penyimpanan, pemindahan dan pencampuran produk petroleum dilaksanakan dengan selamat dan teratur. “Operasi sedemikian memerlukan peralatan yang sesuai, ujian kualiti dan dokumentasi bagi memastikan bahan api memenuhi spesifikasi serta selamat digunakan. “Dokumentasi yang lengkap serta prosedur telus juga penting untuk melindungi hasil kerajaan, memberi kepastian kepada pemain industri dan menarik lebih banyak pelaburan dalam aktiviti bernilai tambah tinggi,” katanya.

OSLO: Norway’s US$2.3 trillion sovereign wealth fund, the world’s largest, reported on Thursday a loss of 278 billion Norwegian crowns (US$29.71 billion) for the third quarter, with a return of minus 0.5% on its global investments. “The fund’s return was close to flat, ending slightly negative as rising interest rates led to weaker results on our fixed-income investments,” deputy CEO Trond Grande said in a statement. Investing the Norwegian state’s revenues from oil and gas production, the fund owns on average 1.5% of all listed companies globally, making it the world’s largest single investor. Overall, the fund is invested in some 7,100 companies as well as bonds, property and renewable energy projects.

A three-member bench comprising Justices Choo Kah Sing, K Muniandy and Latifah Tahar ruled that the High Court had erred in granting bail to M Alagesan despite a statutory prohibition under the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 (Act 234). The bench also ordered the RM150,000 bail money to be returned to a member of Alagesan’s family. Choo said Section 41B of Act 234 expressly prohibits bail for offences punishable by death or imprisonment exceeding five years, notwithstanding any other written law or rule of law to the contrary. “The High Court also erred in relying on Section 388 of the Criminal Procedure Code (CPC) to grant bail to Alagesan when a law expressly prohibits bail,” he said. However, the court expressed sympathy for Alagesan and directed that his trial, scheduled to begin at the Shah Alam High Court on Feb 17 next year, be expedited and concluded by the end of this year if possible. The bench also ordered that Alagesan be placed in Sungai Buloh prison’s hospital unit until his trial concludes. Alagesan, 44, was charged with trafficking 6.2kg of cannabis on a village road near Lot 24 in Kampung KL Tin, Kalumpang, Kuala Kubu Baharu, Hulu Selangor, on Feb 7, 2024. If convicted, he faces the death penalty or imprisonment of 30 to 40 years, with at least 12 strokes of the rotan. On Sept 23, 2024, the High Court granted him bail under Section 388 of the CPC, subject to conditions including monthly police reporting, surrender of his passport, a ban on contacting prosecution witnesses and a curfew from 7pm to 7am. Deputy public prosecutor Hafizah Johor Ariff Johor today argued that Section 41B of Act 234 imposed an absolute bar on bail and overrode Section 388 of the CPC, which allows bail in certain cases involving sick or infirm accused persons. She said Alagesan’s disability did not justify overriding the statutory prohibition and accused the High Court of wrongly placing the burden on the prosecution to prove that prison facilities could meet his needs. Hafizah warned that allowing exceptions could undermine Parliament’s intention to deny bail in serious drug cases and encourage similar applications by other accused persons. Lawyer Naran Singh, assisted by Amrick Singh Sandhu, argued that the prohibition was unconstitutional because judicial power and the separation of powers formed part of the Federal Constitution’s basic structure. “Parliament cannot completely remove the judiciary’s power to decide whether bail should be granted, as doing so would undermine judicial independence,” he said. Naran urged the court to interpret Section 41B of Act 234 purposively to allow bail in exceptional circumstances, stressing that Alagesan remained innocent until proven guilty. He said Alagesan was paralysed from the waist down and used a wheelchair. However, he said, prison authorities had previously failed to provide essential facilities, including a seated toilet and suitable equipment for his personal care.

SYDNEY, Oct 22 (Bernama-Xinhua) -- Researchers have warned of a global decline in childhood measles vaccination rates since the COVID-19 pandemic, contributing to a resurgence of the highly contagious disease, reported Xinhua. Routine vaccine programme disruptions and under-resourced health systems are driving the global decline, with estimated measles cases among children under five rising to 15.6 million worldwide in 2023, a 40 per cent increase from 2019, according to a statement released on Thursday by Australia's University of Queensland (UQ). The study, published in Nature Medicine, examined measles cases, deaths and vaccination gaps among children under five across 204 countries and territories from 1990 to 2023. Associate Professor Benn Sartorius from UQ's Frazer Institute said the resurgence coincided with pandemic-related disruptions to immunisation programmes, health systems and funding, reversing decades of progress, with measles cases falling nearly 80 per cent worldwide between 1990 and 2019. An estimated 23.7 million infants, or one in five worldwide, missed their first measles vaccine dose in 2023. Sub-Saharan Africa accounted for 50 per cent of the missed doses, followed by South Asia at 20 per cent, Sartorius said, adding that the study's data could help authorities identify under-vaccinated populations to prevent future outbreaks. -- BERNAMA-XINHUA BERNAMA provides up-to-date authentic and comprehensive news and information which are disseminated via BERNAMA Wires; www.bernama.com; BERNAMA TV on Astro 502, unifi TV 631 and MYTV 121 channels and BERNAMA Radio on FM93.9 (Klang Valley), FM107.5 (Johor Bahru), FM107.9 (Kota Kinabalu) and FM100.9 (Kuching) frequencies. KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 (Bernama) -- The Developing Eight (D-8) Organisation for Economic Cooperation and the Commission on Science and Technology for Sustainable Development in the South (COMSATS) have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to strengthen cooperation in science, technology, innovation and sustainable development. In a press release issued on Wednesday (Oct 21), the D-8 said the MoU was signed during a virtual ceremony by D-8 Secretary-General Sohail Mahmood and COMSATS Executive Director Dr Mohammad Nafees Zakaria. The agreement covers six priority areas: agriculture and food security; digital transformation, cybersecurity and information and communication technology (ICT); climate change and environmental sustainability; energy security; industry; and public health. Under the MoU, both organisations will explore joint research and development, capacity-building programmes, exchanges of experts and scientists, technology transfer, knowledge-sharing, business development activities, workshops and training initiatives. Sohail said science, technology and innovation were increasingly important in promoting economic competitiveness, sustainable development and resilience among developing countries. “The partnership being forged between the two organisations would provide an important platform for translating scientific knowledge and technological expertise into practical solutions that address the development priorities of their respective member states,” he said. He also highlighted the importance of a results-oriented approach focused on institutional capacity-building, innovation, technology transfer and practical joint initiatives that deliver tangible benefits to member states. Meanwhile, Mohammad Nafees highlighted COMSATS’ role in promoting scientific and technological cooperation among developing countries. He said COMSATS comprised 27 member states across Asia, Africa, and Latin America and the Caribbean, supported by a network of 25 Centres of Excellence and scientific and technical expertise from various countries. D-8 and COMSATS share six member states: Bangladesh, Egypt, Iran, Nigeria, Pakistan and Turkiye, providing a foundation for closer institutional collaboration and joint initiatives in areas of mutual interest. Both organisations have designated focal persons to facilitate coordination and implementation of the MoU, reaffirming their commitment to South-South cooperation, institutional capacity-building, innovation and technology transfer. The partnership aims to advance scientific and technological capabilities and promote inclusive economic growth and sustainable development across their member states. -- BERNAMA BERNAMA provides up-to-date authentic and comprehensive news and information which are disseminated via BERNAMA Wires; www.bernama.com; BERNAMA TV on Astro 502, unifi TV 631 and MYTV 121 channels and BERNAMA Radio on FM93.9 (Klang Valley), FM107.5 (Johor Bahru), FM107.9 (Kota Kinabalu) and FM100.9 (Kuching) frequencies. SHAH ALAM, Oct 22 (Bernama) -- The Selangor government is accelerating flood mitigation works, including dredging and widening a 54-kilometre stretch of the Klang River, to reduce flood risks. State executive councillor for infrastructure and agriculture Datuk Izham Hashim said the project faced challenges from accumulated solid waste and thick sediment deposits following two decades without comprehensive maintenance. “The original five-year timeline could be shortened to 18 months or two years following the approval of additional federal projects upstream and downstream," he said after closing the Selangor Friends of Rivers (FOR) Workshop 2026 here today. Izham said dredging operations had been hampered by debris, including bicycle frames, mattresses and heavy textiles, which damaged equipment. Nevertheless, the works had begun reducing flood risks, while the river's water depth had increased from one metre to four metres. Izham said federal funding worth hundreds of millions of ringgit for floodwall construction had helped reduce the state's remaining expenditure to just over RM200 million. He said river conservation efforts were also supported by 58 active FOR community groups, which help authorities monitor river reserves and report environmental violations. Izham said a mobile app introduced by the Selangor Water Management Authority (LUAS) in 2022 has also streamlined reporting and enforcement. He warned that property owners allowing illegal dumping on their premises could face legal action, including land forfeiture. Nearly 300 participants attended the workshop to strengthen community involvement in river conservation. -- BERNAMA BERNAMA provides up-to-date authentic and comprehensive news and information which are disseminated via BERNAMA Wires; www.bernama.com; BERNAMA TV on Astro 502, unifi TV 631 and MYTV 121 channels and BERNAMA Radio on FM93.9 (Klang Valley), FM107.5 (Johor Bahru), FM107.9 (Kota Kinabalu) and FM100.9 (Kuching) frequencies. KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 (Bernama) -- YYForce Inc (YYForce), a workforce solutions provider, has announced its strategic plans to develop Workforce OS, a robotics operating system built on NVIDIA computing and robotics technology, starting with deployments in hotels. YYForce in a statement said it is designed to let human workers operate alongside artificial intelligence (AI)-powered robots, including Unitree humanoid robots and other service robots. “Our strategic objective is to own the software intelligence layer that makes diverse commercial robots truly useful in live business environments. “By combining NVIDIA’s industry-defining physical AI computing stack with versatile hardware like Unitree humanoid platforms, we aim to bridge the gap between simulation and real-world execution,” said YYForce Chief Executive Officer, Mike Fu. YYForce plans a phased roll-out in hotel settings. Over the first two months, it aims to set up robot navigation and guest-facing concierge services, followed by robotic arms for food and beverage service from months two to four. By month six, it plans to run multi-robot operations, including pilot Unitree humanoid robots, at hotel banquets and events. In the longer term, it aims to extend the system to facility maintenance and industrial cleaning. Workforce OS is designed to work across different robot hardware, covering computer vision, navigation, robotic arm control, conversational interaction and fleet management. It will use NVIDIA Jetson edge AI modules on the robots for real-time perception and control and NVIDIA’s Isaac Sim and Project GR00T to train robots in simulation before real-world deployment. KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 (Bernama) -- A pilot project to improve wayfinding signage will be implemented at the Masjid Jamek Light Rail Transit (LRT) station and could be expanded across the rail network if successful, says Transport Minister Anthony Loke. He said the initiative is one of four components under Phase Three of the Masjid Jamek LRT Station Beautification Project, which involves an investment of RM5 million by Prasarana Malaysia Berhad. He added that the upgraded navigation system covers signage across the station to facilitate smoother passenger movement, including for foreign tourists. “The station will undergo a wayfinding upgrade, which includes all directional signs. “If this pilot is successful and well received, the signage design will be expanded to all other stations,” he told reporters after launching the project here today. Also present were Kuala Lumpur Mayor Datuk Seri Fadlun Mak Ujud, Prasarana Group Acting President and Chief Operating Officer Dr Prodyut Dutt, and Think City Managing Director Datuk Hamdan Abdul Majeed. Loke said the upgrade also entails improving street lighting along Jalan Tun Perak following passenger feedback regarding poorly lit areas outside the station at night. He said the Jalan Benteng area will be upgraded to feature cafe and recreational spaces, alongside additional platform greenery to create a cooler and more pleasant environment. Court grants PN reprieve from ROS deregistration Perikatan Nasional can proceed with its plans to contest the Malacca state election after the Kuala Lumpur High Court today granted a stay on the Registrar of Societies’ (ROS) decision to deregister the opposition pact. Perikatan Nasional can proceed with its plans to contest the Malacca state election after the Kuala Lumpur High Court today granted a stay on the Registrar of Societies’ (ROS) decision to deregister the opposition pact. The court decision came after the ROS revoked PN’s registration on Tuesday after deeming the coalition’s response to its show-cause notice unsatisfactory. The stay was granted as PN’s previous application sought to restrain the ROS from taking further action against the coalition. The court found that the deregistration risked undermining the judicial review application before it could be decided upon. However, judge Azizan Arshad said the stay would remain in force pending PN’s judicial review challenging the deregistration. “At this stage, the court will not decide whether the respondent’s action of deregistering is valid, or whether it is exempt from judicial review. “The implications or the validity of the exercise of such power may still be challenged in a separate proceeding. “A stay on the deregistration is granted until the substantive matter is dealt with in the judicial review proper,” Azizan said today after hearing the arguments from both sides' lawyers. The high court judge said that exceptional circumstances warranted the stay, taking into account PN’s role in politics and the potential implications for its rights as elected representatives and state governments. “The court finds that there is no prejudice if the stay were granted, as the ongoing oversight of PN’s political activities can still be maintained and enforced,” he added. 30-day deadline Earlier, senior federal counsel Nurhafizza Azizan argued that PN needed to file a fresh judicial review application, as the ROS had not deregistered the coalition when the original application was filed, rendering the matter academic. However, PN’s counsel Azhar Azizan Harun maintained that the application remained relevant, as one of the reliefs sought was an order restraining the ROS from deregistering the coalition pending the judicial review’s disposal. Azhar also argued that the ROS had acted prematurely by deregistering PN before the 30-day period stipulated in its show-cause notice had expired. “In their haste to halt these proceedings, they breached their own timeline of 30 days stipulated in the notice. The deregistration should take place 30 days after the notice date. This is a statutory requirement,” Azhar said. PN’s deregistration stemmed from a complaint from Bersatu, which was at loggerheads with PAS over the coalition’s direction. On Sept 22, PN received a show-cause notice from the ROS for failing to invite Bersatu to a coalition supreme council meeting on July 16. The following day, it was ordered to suspend activities under the PN name. PN secretary-general Takiyuddin Hassan slammed ROS on Sept 24, saying the deregistration notice was issued in bad faith to apply political pressure. PN then filed a judicial review at the Kuala Lumpur High Court to seek clarity on its status and quash the ROS actions. Among the applicants are Takiyuddin, alongside the secretaries-general of its component parties, including Saifuddin Abdullah (Wawasan Negara), Sazmi Miah (Pejuang), Wong Chia Zhen (Gerakan), and Satish Kumar (MIPP). ROS director-general Zulfikar Ahmad and Home Minister Saifuddin Nasution Ismail were named as respondents.
